newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition calls strike, markets slump.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition calls strike, markets slump.

text.p: Bangladesh financial markets slumped on Wednesday ahead of a national half-day strike called by the main opposition party.
The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia called Thursday's work stoppage to protest what it says is an "anti-people" budget passed by parliament on Monday.
News of the strike sent shares on the Dhaka Stock Exchange tumbling and prompted importers to unload the local taka currency and buy dollars, dealers said.
The DSE index lost 1.18 percent, or 13.2 points, to end at 1,098.35.
"It has certainly affected the market. It was depressed and the (stock) prices fell amid selling pressure," said broker Abdul Rashid of Abdul Rasid & Co.
But he said improving economic fundamentals in Bangladesh and signs of weak public support for the strike would likely lend the markets support.
"The market has got to improve because the country's economic condition is improving," Rashid said.
"The government is doing its best to improve the country's economy. I don't think the general people will support the opposition protest."

The BNP had sought the withdrawal of a 2.5 percent development tax on imports and some locally produced goods and services, which Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria proposed when unveiling the budget last month.
BNP Secretary General Abdul Mannan said on Tuesday -- the first day of Bangladesh's fiscal 1997/98 year -- the budget was against the interests of the country.
"The budget will deter investment and it will make the country dependent on others," he told party supporters.
